true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Compare postMessage origins exactly

A substring check accepts origins that are merely prefixes of the configured origin. For example, discourseUrl='https://forum.example.com/' accepts a message from 'https://forum.example.co'. A window on that different domain with a reference to the embedding page can send resize messages to hide or stretch the comments iframe. Compare against the parsed, exact Discourse origin and verify that e.source is the iframe's contentWindow.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Remove the incomplete postfix condition from the closing tag

This tag emits `end if` without a condition instead of closing the block with `end`. The incomplete Ruby statement breaks compilation of the ERB template, so requests for URLs with an existing TopicEmbed fail when rendering the discussion. The controller specs do not render views and therefore do not catch this.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Handle RSS description fields and entries without content

Valid RSS items commonly provide their body through description or content:encoded rather than the Atom content field; Atom entries can also contain only summary. For those entries, i.content is nil and calling scrub raises NoMethodError, aborting the entire feed import. Select the available body field and handle missing content explicitly. The current specs only test whether poll_feed is called, not whether a real feed can be imported.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate:
Defer post-creation jobs until the outer transaction commits

PostCreator.create enqueues process_post and feature_topic_users before returning. Wrapping it in this additional Topic.transaction means those jobs are now published while the new topic and post remain uncommitted. A fast worker can execute them before their records are visible, causing processing to fail or be skipped; a subsequent rollback also leaves jobs for nonexistent records. Preserve the atomic import but defer job publication until the enclosing transaction commits.

Preserve exported thread timestamps during Disqus imports

The previous PostCreator call supplied the exported thread's created_at value. TopicEmbed.import_remote does not forward a creation timestamp, so historical topics and their first posts are now dated at import time while their replies still use the original exported dates. This corrupts discussion chronology and makes old threads appear newly created. Pass the thread timestamp through the new import API.

Resolve relative references using the source URL

The string concatenation mishandles standard URL references. For an article at https://blog.example/posts/one, src='//cdn.example/image.png' becomes https://blog.example/cdn.example/image.png, while href='two.html' is left unchanged and resolves against the forum instead of the source article. Both links and images can therefore break after import. Resolve references against the complete source URI rather than stripping leading slashes and prepending the host.

Sanitize HTML even when bypassing Markdown rendering

The new raw_html mode returns raw content without sanitization. PollFeed passes external feed content into this mode through TopicEmbed.import, and Nokogiri parsing only rewrites URLs—it preserves scripts, event handlers, and unsafe link schemes. For example, an imported image with an onerror handler becomes executable stored HTML in the forum's origin. Edits to these posts retain the same bypass. Keep an HTML sanitization step on every cook.

Set the retrieval marker and its expiry atomically

SETNX and EXPIRE are separate operations. If the worker exits after SETNX succeeds but before EXPIRE runs, the marker remains indefinitely and retrieved_recently? suppresses every subsequent retrieval of that URL. Without feed polling, the embed stays on the loading page permanently despite repeated requests. Create the marker with its expiry in one atomic Redis operation.

Validate redirect destinations before fetching them

TopicRetriever checks the initial URL's hostname, but open-uri follows redirects here without rechecking the destination. An allowed-host URL that redirects to another host, including an internal HTTP service, bypasses the embed-host allowlist; the server fetches that response and may publish its content as the configured import user. Validate each redirect target before issuing the next request rather than following redirects unchecked.

-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.

false_positives.candidate:
Preserve right-alignment in the legacy flexbox fallback

The new `flexbox()` mixin selects `display: -webkit-box` on browsers such as stock Android 4.0–4.3 and Safari 6.0, but that older box model does not distribute free space through `margin-left: auto`. With `float: right` removed and no corresponding `box-flex` or `box-pack` rule, the navigation panel sits immediately after the logo/topic information instead of at the right edge. Its right-anchored dropdowns move left as well, potentially placing the wide search menu partly offscreen. Add an old-box-compatible distribution rule or retain a working float fallback for those browsers.

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Do not replace an existing native refresh token with a placeholder

The placeholder assignment also runs when credential syncing is disabled. Office365's response schema explicitly allows a refresh response without a replacement `refresh_token`, and its caller merges the parsed response into the existing credentials. Such a response now overwrites the valid stored refresh token with the literal `refresh_token`, making the next refresh fail. Leave an omitted native refresh token unset so the caller can preserve the existing value.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Define actual expiry fields instead of computed Zod object keys

Calling `toString()` on these Zod schemas produces the literal key `[object Object]`, not a wildcard property definition; the second computed property also overwrites the first. Because Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, a synced response containing `expires_in`, `expiry_date`, and `refresh_token` loses those fields. Zoom then computes a NaN expiry, and Office365 cannot update its expiry correctly. Define and preserve the actual supported response fields.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns `{ success: true, data: credentials }`, whereas the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse` returned the credentials themselves. Passing this result directly to `prisma.credential.update` nests all token fields under `key.data`. This also happens with syncing disabled: after an ordinary refresh, subsequent calendar operations no longer find the expected root-level OAuth fields. Persist the result's `data` instead.

true_positives.matched_candidate:
Pass the credential owner's user ID to the sync endpoint

The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is a user ID, but this call passes the credential row's primary key. The helper sends that value as `calcomUserId`, so a credential whose ID differs from its owner's ID requests another user's tokens or fails lookup. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

false_positives.candidate:
Authenticate outbound credential-sync requests

This token-retrieval POST contains only a user ID and app slug; it attaches no secret, signature, or other authentication. A public sync endpoint accepting this protocol cannot distinguish Cal from another caller requesting the same user's bearer token, while an endpoint requiring the configured shared secret will reject these calls. Add authenticated server-to-server requests, for example using the configured secret header, rather than relying on enumerable identifiers.

Clear the invalid flag when replacing invalidated credentials

The existing-credential branch updates only `key`. Google, Zoom, and Webex mark credentials `invalid: true` after unrecoverable authentication failures, so pushing fresh valid credentials through this webhook leaves the integration marked invalid despite returning success. Reset the invalid state when accepting a valid replacement so the parent store can reconnect an invalidated integration.

Do not delete externally managed Lark credentials based on local refresh tokens

Before reaching the new sync request, `refreshAccessToken` still deletes the credential if its local refresh token is absent or expired. With external credential management, the parent can hold a valid rotated refresh token even when Cal's local copy is missing or stale. Cal then deletes a recoverable integration without consulting the source of truth. Keep the local refresh-token validation and deletion inside the native-provider fallback.

Handle the access-token-only sync response in Webex

After routing Webex refreshes to the external endpoint, the response is still validated with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema`, which requires scope, token type, refresh token, and refresh-token expiry. An endpoint following the helper's documented access-token/expiry-only response therefore always fails with `Invalid refreshed tokens were returned`. Add a sync-specific parsing and merge path that does not require the parent to disclose its refresh token.

Import Prisma before updating Salesforce credentials

The new credential update references `prisma`, but this file never imports or declares it. Type-checking fails with `Cannot find name 'prisma'`; if type-checking is bypassed, a successful token refresh throws a ReferenceError before returning the Salesforce connection. Import the shared Prisma client.

Make initial webhook delivery idempotent under concurrency

The lookup and creation are separate operations. Two simultaneous deliveries for the same user and app can both find no credential and then create separate rows. Later deliveries update only one row through `findFirst`, leaving duplicate integrations with stale credentials. Serialize creation for the same sync identity or introduce a database-enforced idempotency mechanism rather than relying on this check-then-create sequence.

Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint

The new Salesforce refresh always posts directly to Salesforce and never calls `refreshOAuthTokens`. Consequently, enabling sharing and setting `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` has no effect on Salesforce token retrieval: Cal still requires a locally usable refresh token and refreshes independently of the parent store. Externally managed credentials whose refresh token is retained by the parent cannot work through this path.

Send Zoom's canonical app slug

The refresh request sends `appSlug=zoomvideo`, but Zoom credentials are installed with `appId: "zoom"`, and the webhook identifies apps by that canonical slug. A parent store looking up the synced Zoom integration by the supplied slug will not find it. Pass `zoom` rather than the integration directory/API route name.

true_positives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
An empty Prisma update does not refresh updatedAt

updateManyByCredentialId forwards this empty object directly to Prisma. Prisma does not bump an @updatedAt field when the update data is empty, so this call leaves SelectedCalendar.updatedAt unchanged after every cache refresh instead of recording the refresh time as intended. Supply updatedAt explicitly, or remove this unused timestamp-tracking call if CalendarCache.updatedAt is the sole freshness marker.

true_positives.matched_candidate:
Make the environment update work with GNU sed

The sed -i '' invocation uses BSD/macOS syntax and fails with GNU sed. On Linux, once GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists, rerunning this helper leaves the old URL in place but still prints that it was updated successfully. Subsequent Google Calendar watches consequently use the stale tunnel endpoint. Use a portable replacement strategy or handle both sed variants, and check the command's exit status before reporting success.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

false_positives.candidate:
Invalidate cache status after deleting cached data

The delete-cache mutation only invokes the optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates connectedCalendars. The wrapper forwards an optional onChanged callback and disables refetchOnWindowFocus, so deleting the cache can leave the old timestamp and delete action displayed after the success toast. Invalidate viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars after deletion, as the disconnect mutation already does, so the displayed status reflects the database.

Resolve persisted cache records for delegated calendar connections

Connected calendars can use in-memory delegation credentials with negative IDs, while CalendarCache rows belong to persisted credentials. getCachedAvailability explicitly supports this by looking up delegated availability using userId and key, including reusing an existing OAuth connection's cache after delegation is enabled. This new credential-ID-only lookup cannot find those same rows, so cacheUpdatedAt becomes null and the dropdown hides both status and deletion for the delegated connection even while its cached availability is being served. Resolve the user's persisted cache credentials for these connections and use an ownership-checked deletion path for them.

Resolve the environment file relative to the script

ENV_FILE is resolved relative to the caller's working directory, not the script's location. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repository root therefore creates or modifies .env in the repository's parent directory, leaving the application's environment unchanged while reporting success. Derive the repository root from the script's location before selecting the environment file.

Keep the registered metric-alert handler instantiable

MetricAlertDetectorHandler now inherits four abstract members without implementing them: counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data. MetricAlertFire still registers this class, and Detector.detector_handler instantiates it unconditionally. Build the expected occurrence for the group being evaluated

The expected occurrence is built for "val1", but the evaluation below uses "group_key". Since build_mock_occurrence_and_event incorporates that argument into the fingerprint, the expected occurrence identifies a different issue from the actual occurrence. true_positives.golden_comment: Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The process type check prevents hung workers from being killed

Workers created by multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process are SpawnProcess instances, not instances of the top-level multiprocessing.Process class. This condition is therefore false for production workers. When a worker is classified as hung, its dictionary entry is replaced without killing it, leaving an untracked process that can resume flushing the same shards and updating the same health/backpressure values as its replacement. Check against SpawnProcess or BaseProcess and stop the old worker before replacing it.

true_positives.golden_comment: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Continue worker cleanup after the join deadline expires

If waiting for one flusher exhausts the timeout, this break skips termination of every remaining worker. It also skips all workers if next_step.join(timeout) consumes the deadline. Setting stopped only helps workers that return to the top of their loop; workers blocked in Redis or Kafka calls can remain alive after join returns and overlap with replacement flushers following a rebalance. The deadline should stop further waiting, but cleanup must still terminate every outstanding child.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.

true_positives.golden_comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.

Make the device-limit check and admission atomic
